subject: math
cluster: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations

items.prompt:
The AA criterion proves two triangles are:
A) Congruent
B) Similar
C) Equal in area
D) Right triangles

AA requires how many pairs of equal angles?
A) One
B) Two
C) Three
D) Zero

Two triangles both have angles $30°$ and $90°$. They are:
A) Not similar
B) Similar
C) Congruent only
D) Equilateral

steps: Two matching angle pairs give similarity by AA.

items.prompt:
If two angles of one triangle equal two of another, the third angles are:
A) Different
B) Equal
C) Supplementary
D) Zero

steps: The angle sum forces the third to match.

items.prompt:
Does AA prove congruence?
A) Yes
B) No, only similarity
C) Only for right triangles
D) Only for equilateral triangles

steps: No side is fixed, so only similarity.

items.prompt:
Are all equilateral triangles similar?
A) No
B) Yes
C) Only congruent ones
D) Only large ones

steps: All have three $60°$ angles, so AA applies.

items.prompt:
Two right triangles each also have a $40°$ angle. They are:
A) Not similar
B) Similar by AA
C) Congruent
D) Equilateral

steps: $90°$ and $40°$ match, so AA gives similarity.

items.prompt:
Why is AA enough for similarity but not congruence?
A) It fixes size but not shape
B) It fixes shape but not size
C) It fixes neither
D) It fixes both
items.answer: B) It fixes shape but not size

steps: AA determines the angles (shape) but no side (size).
